title_en: Sanpu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. v. Far East Smart Energy Co., Ltd., et al. — third-party revocation action
ruling_gist_en: Although the equity transfer price between shareholders of a limited liability company referenced the operating conditions of the target company, the target company is not bound by the equity transfer contract in terms of its conclusion and performance. Therefore, the failure of the target company to participate in the lawsuit between the parties to the equity transfer does not constitute a ground for revocation under the law. The third-party revocation action filed by the target company shall be dismissed in accordance with law.
keywords_en: civil; third-party revocation action; dispute over equity transfer; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Qinghai Province; legal person; Civil Procedure Law; Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; standing to bring a third-party revocation action; legal interest; whether there is fault in not participating in the lawsuit; reversal; equity transfer; debts of the target company
full_text_en:
Sanpu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. v. Far East Wisdom Energy Co., Ltd. et al. — third-party revocation action

[Ruling Gist]

Although the price of equity transfer between shareholders of a limited liability company reflects the operating conditions of the target company, the target company is not bound by the conclusion and performance of the equity transfer contract. Therefore, the target company's failure to participate in the lawsuit between the parties to the equity transfer does not constitute a ground for revocation that should be granted by law, and the target company's request for a third-party revocation action should be dismissed.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2022) Supreme People's Court Final Civil Judgment No. 50

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Far East Wisdom Energy Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 1202-8, 12th Floor, Innovation and Entrepreneurship Building, No. 7 South Shandong Road, Chengdong District, Xining City, Qinghai Province.

Legal Representative: Jiang Xipei, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yu, Attorney at Beijing Dacheng Law Offices.

Agent ad litem: Tang Xiaoqin, Attorney at Beijing Dacheng Law Offices.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Sanpu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 12 Erjing Road, Biological Park, Chengbei District, Xining City, Qinghai Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Yuanyuan, Executive Director.

Agent ad litem: Xia Jianan, Attorney at Beijing Zhongwen Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Tibet Rong'en Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: Zangqing Industrial Park, Golmud City, Qinghai Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Xuefeng, Executive Director.

Agent ad litem: Chen Lin, Attorney at Shanghai Duan & Duan (Chengdu) Law Office.

Far East Wisdom Energy Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Far East Wisdom Company), the appellant, filed an appeal with this Court against the civil judgment (2021) Qingmin No. 1 of the Qinghai High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the Qinghai High Court) in the case of the third-party revocation action brought by the appellee, Sanpu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sanpu Company), against the appellant and the defendant at first instance, Tibet Rong'en Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tibet Rong'en Company). This Court accepted the case on February 14, 2022. After acceptance, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing. Wang Yu and Tang Xiaoqin, agents ad litem of Far East Wisdom Company, Xia Jianan, agent ad litem of Sanpu Company, and Chen Lin, agent ad litem of Tibet Rong'en Company, appeared in court. This case is now concluded.

Far East Wisdom Company appealed with the following requests: 1. to set aside Items 1 and 2 of the civil judgment (2021) Qingmin No. 1 of the first instance court, and to amend the judgment to dismiss all claims of Sanpu Company; 2. to order Sanpu Company to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances. Facts and grounds: (1) The first instance court's case filing procedure was illegal and the application of law was erroneous. According to Article 293 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Revised in 2020), the case filing procedure for a third-party revocation action is different from ordinary civil cases and is not subject to the case filing registration system. The first instance court accepted the case immediately upon receipt of Sanpu Company's complaint, thereby depriving Far East Wisdom Company of the right to submit written opinions before filing, which violated the spirit of substantive review and strict case filing for third-party revocation actions. (2) Sanpu Company does not have the standing to initiate a third-party revocation action. 1. Sanpu Company does not have a legal interest in the case. The "legal interest" as provided in paragraph 2 of Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Revised in 2017) should refer to situations where there is a directly related legal relationship and the interests are materially affected in fact. The civil judgments (2020) Qingmin Zhong No. 291 and (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 52 are disputes over an equity transfer contract between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company. The "Equity Acquisition Agreement" explicitly stipulates that Far East Wisdom Company has the right to claim RMB 50 million from Tibet Rong'en Company. Tibet Rong'en Company conducted necessary due diligence when acquiring the target company, confirmed that the target company had this RMB 50 million debt, and agreed on a specific payment schedule for the RMB 50 million. The RMB 50 million is part of the equity transfer price under the Equity Acquisition Agreement, and the actual payer is Tibet Rong'en Company. Sanpu Company is not a party to the Equity Acquisition Agreement and has no rights or obligations under that legal relationship. The original effective judgment only binds Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company; the main text of the effective judgment does not determine or directly affect the rights and obligations of Sanpu Company. There is no legal interest between the judgment and Sanpu Company, and Sanpu Company's civil rights and interests have not been actually harmed. 2. The Equity Acquisition Agreement did not impose additional debts on Sanpu Company. Sanpu Company's RMB 50 million liability was calculated by Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company in the Equity Acquisition Agreement based on pre-existing claims and debts, and did not impose any new debt on Sanpu Company, nor did it require Sanpu Company to incur debt. The Equity Acquisition Agreement not only did not impose a RMB 50 million debt on Sanpu Company, but in many places exempted Sanpu Company from debts it might still owe to Far East Wisdom Company, or provided that Far East Wisdom Company would assume debts, payments, and compensation liabilities that Sanpu Company might bear. The Equity Acquisition Agreement existed on file when the equity was changed, and its contents were publicly available. Sanpu Company went through the industrial and commercial change registration, and thus should have been aware of the RMB 50 million and accepted the payment method. The debt involved was confirmed by an audit report, and the claim that Sanpu Company's financial statements were not provided does not hold. 3. Sanpu Company does not enjoy the civil rights and interests that can be protected by a third-party revocation action. Civil rights and interests generally refer to the civil rights and interests stipulated in Article 2 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China and the creditor's rights given special protection by law. The civil rights and interests claimed by Sanpu Company in this case are ordinary creditor-debtor relationships, which are not within the scope of protection of a third-party revocation action. Tibet Rong'en Company admitted that after the transfer of Sanpu Company's equity, Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company carried out handover of Sanpu Company's financial matters, including Sanpu Company's balance sheet and profit statement as of December 26, 2015, which bore Sanpu Company's seal. The Equity Acquisition Agreement did not require a borrowing agreement between Tibet Rong'en Company and Sanpu Company, but rather Tibet Rong'en Company joined the debt between Sanpu Company and Far East Wisdom Company, assuming the obligation to repay Far East Wisdom Company. (3) Sanpu Company was fully aware of the entire litigation in the other case and was at significant fault for failing to exercise its litigation rights, failing to participate in the lawsuit between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company, and thus does not meet the procedural requirements for initiating a third-party revocation action. 1. Sanpu Company knew all the circumstances of the dispute in this case. This case and the related cases all stem from the Equity Acquisition Agreement between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company. The equity transfer dispute between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company and the shareholder capital contribution dispute between Sanpu Company and Far East Wisdom Company were heard almost simultaneously. Moreover, when the Xining Intermediate People's Court of Qinghai Province (hereinafter referred to as the Xining Intermediate Court) heard the equity transfer dispute between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company in 2016, the legal representatives of both Tibet Rong'en Company and Sanpu Company were Zhang Xuefeng. In the shareholder capital contribution dispute between Sanpu Company and Far East Wisdom Company, Sanpu Company recognized the authenticity of the first-instance judgment in the Far East Wisdom Company v. Tibet Rong'en Company dispute provided by Far East Wisdom Company, and Sanpu Company's legal representative participated in the trial. The two former legal representatives of Sanpu Company were fully aware of the facts, development, and litigation circumstances of the dispute between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company involving RMB 50 million under the Equity Acquisition Agreement. 2. Sanpu Company was clearly at fault for failing to participate in the lawsuit. From 2016 to when Sanpu Company filed this third-party revocation action, a period of five years, the related cases went through multiple trials. Sanpu Company knew the original lawsuit was ongoing but did not apply to participate. It failed to fulfill the burden of proof under Article 292 (2020 revision) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and its claims should be dismissed. 3. The related cases among Tibet Rong'en Company, Far East Wisdom Company, and Sanpu Company were remanded for retrial multiple times. Sanpu Company was fully capable of judging the relationship between the litigation outcome and its own interests, but Sanpu Company voluntarily gave up its litigation rights solely due to an erroneous judgment of the litigation outcome. Now it initiates this lawsuit on the ground that it could not judge whether it was related to the case, which is clearly inconsistent with the facts. The first instance court's finding that a third party without independent claims, when the people's court does not notify it to participate in the lawsuit and the parties do not apply for its participation, generally cannot be deemed to be at significant fault was erroneous.

Sanpu Company argued in response: (1) The result of the civil judgment (2020) Qingmin Zhong No. 291 has a legal interest in Sanpu Company and has harmed Sanpu Company's civil rights and interests. Sanpu Company meets the standing and substantive conditions for a third-party revocation action and has the right to initiate this lawsuit. 1. The civil judgment (2020) Qingmin Zhong No. 291 ordered Tibet Rong'en Company to pay RMB 50 million to Far East Wisdom Company based on the Equity Acquisition Agreement. This amount represented the debt owed by Sanpu Company to Far East Wisdom Company and its affiliates, and was to be paid by Tibet Rong'en Company to Far East Wisdom Company after borrowing from Sanpu Company. The result of the effective judgment has an obvious legal interest in Sanpu Company, and Sanpu Company is a third party without independent claims. 2. In the effective judgment of the other case, without Sanpu Company participating in the conclusion of the Equity Acquisition Agreement or participating in the trial, the court failed to examine the basic facts such as whether Sanpu Company owed money and the amount of the debt, and found that Sanpu Company owed RMB 50 million to Far East Wisdom Company and its affiliates and ordered Tibet Rong'en Company to pay it to Far East Wisdom Company. This was clearly erroneous and harmed Sanpu Company's civil rights and interests. 3. The effective judgment of the other case wrongfully imposed a debt on Sanpu Company and exposed Sanpu Company to massive debt recovery, harming Sanpu Company's property rights and interests. Sanpu Company initiated this third-party revocation action because the erroneous effective judgment of the other case caused it to bear a RMB 50 million debt and harmed its property rights and interests, which falls within the scope of civil rights and interests protected by law for a third-party revocation action. Far East Wisdom Company's argument that the civil rights and interests claimed by Sanpu Company are ordinary creditor-debtor relationships not protected by a third-party revocation action is inconsistent with the facts of this case and has no legal basis. (2) According to the relevant guidance of the Supreme People's Court, Sanpu Company, as a third party without independent claims in the effective judgment of the other case, did not have a significant fault in failing to participate in the lawsuit and meets the procedural conditions for initiating a third-party revocation action. 1. As a third party without independent claims, even if Sanpu Company knew the litigation existed, if the people's court did not notify it to participate and the parties did not apply for its participation, it generally cannot be deemed to have significant fault. Therefore, Sanpu Company meets the procedural conditions for initiating a third-party revocation action. 2. Far East Wisdom Company claims Sanpu Company had significant fault and should bear the burden of proving that Sanpu Company was fully aware of the other case and could judge the relationship between the litigation outcome and its interests. In this case, Far East Wisdom Company failed to meet its burden of proof, so Sanpu Company cannot be deemed to have significant fault. 3. Sanpu Company's civil rights and interests were harmed by the erroneous judgment in the other case, and it has no other judicial remedy except initiating this third-party revocation action. The first instance court's finding that "considering that the legal knowledge and litigation ability of current litigation parties are still not high, requiring the third party to be without fault would be detrimental to protecting the lawful rights and interests of third parties outside the case" is consistent with the relevant guidance of the Supreme People's Court and reflects the legislative value of third-party revocation actions, and should be upheld. (3) Although the first instance court did not serve the complaint on Far East Wisdom Company before filing, Far East Wisdom Company participated in the first instance trial of this case and fully exercised its litigation rights. Its right to submit written opinions was not substantially harmed. The failure to serve the complaint and evidence materials before filing was not a serious procedural violation and did not hinder Far East Wisdom Company's litigation rights after the case was accepted. Therefore, the procedure did not affect the outcome of this case. Moreover, during the four-month trial period at the first instance, Far East Wisdom Company never raised an objection to the case filing procedure. Far East Wisdom Company's ground of appeal that the first instance court's case filing procedure was illegal by depriving it of the right to submit written opinions cannot stand. Sanpu Company requests that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be upheld.

Tibet Rong'en Company argued in response: (1) Whether the first instance court served the complaint before or after filing does not affect Far East Wisdom Company's exercise of its rights or the correctness of the judgment. (2) Far East Wisdom Company applied for enforcement against Tibet Rong'en Company based on the civil judgment (2020) Qingmin Zhong No. 291 and has already enforced over RMB 10 million. If the judgment is not revoked, Tibet Rong'en Company will exercise its right of recourse against Sanpu Company. (3) Article 4.1 of the Equity Acquisition Agreement uses terms such as "repay" and "borrowing" to clearly define the nature of the disputed amount as a loan. A loan contract is a practical contract; its formation requires not only a loan agreement but also actual delivery. Since Sanpu Company had no intention to borrow, no loan contract could be formed. The clause stipulates "subject to Sanpu's financial statements," but before the agreement was signed, Tibet Rong'en Company, considering that Far East Wisdom Company was a listed company, did not verify the statements, so the clause provided "estimated not to exceed…" and in Article 11.3 of the agreement, Far East Wisdom Company made a commitment: "The target company's financial statements do not contain any false records." During the signing process, Far East Wisdom Company did not submit the target company's financial statements to Tibet Rong'en Company for confirmation. After signing, not until Far East Wisdom Company received the equity transfer price of RMB 320 million and transferred the electronic financial records to Tibet Rong'en Company did Tibet Rong'en Company discover that the financial statements contained many false records, leading to a series of disputes. Currently, the dispute regarding Tibet Rong'en Company's demand for Far East Wisdom Company to make up the net asset shortfall due to the false financial records is still ongoing. (4) In the first instance, the parties to this case clearly stated that they had never reached a confirmation on the contents of the statements. Far East Wisdom Company's argument that the balance sheet was attached to the Equity Acquisition Agreement and thus the RMB 50 million should be supported is unfounded. (5) Sanpu Company is an independent legal entity, and its free will should be respected. Tibet Rong'en Company did not manipulate Sanpu Company in this litigation. Article 4.1 of the Equity Acquisition Agreement actually proves that Far East Wisdom Company directly disposed of the creditor-debtor relationship with Sanpu Company on behalf of its affiliates.

Sanpu Company filed the following claims with the first instance court: 1. to revoke the civil judgment (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 52 of the Xining Intermediate Court and the civil judgment (2020) Qingmin Zhong No. 291 of the Qinghai High Court in accordance with the law; 2. to confirm in accordance with the law that the clauses (4.1, 6.3, 6.4) in the Equity Acquisition Agreement between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company that impose obligations (debts) on Sanpu Company are invalid. During the first instance trial, Sanpu Company changed its claims to: to revoke Items 1 and 2 of the civil judgment (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 52 of the Xining Intermediate Court and the part of the civil judgment (2020) Qingmin Zhong No. 291 of the Qinghai High Court that upheld Items 1 and 2 of the civil judgment (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 52.

In the equity transfer dispute case (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 52 between Far East Wisdom Company (plaintiff) and Tibet Rong'en Company (defendant), Far East Wisdom Company filed the following claims with the Xining Intermediate Court: 1. Tibet Rong'en Company pay RMB 50 million to Far East Wisdom Company in accordance with the agreement; 2. pay liquidated damages of RMB 36.15 million as agreed (calculated at 0.3% per day of the unpaid amount until full payment, temporarily calculated to July 31, 2016), and bear the litigation costs and attorney fees of RMB 1.25 million; 3. pay other losses of RMB 10,282,448.78.

The Xining Intermediate Court found the following facts: Far East Wisdom Company (Party A) and Tibet Rong'en Company (Party B) signed the "Equity Acquisition Agreement" on October 21, 2015. The agreement provided that Party A would transfer the acquisition target to Party B in accordance with the agreement, and Party B would purchase the acquisition target from Party A in accordance with the agreement. The acquisition target under this agreement was Party A's 100% equity interest in Sanpu Company. The net assets of the target company as of the date of equity transfer would not be less than RMB 240 million; otherwise, Party A would be obligated to make up the difference to Party B. The total liabilities as of the date of equity transfer would not exceed RMB 120 million; otherwise, Party A would repay the difference on behalf of the target company. As of the date of equity transfer, the amounts payable by the target company to Party A and its affiliates would not exceed RMB 100 million, and the amounts receivable by the target company from Party A and its affiliates were estimated not to exceed RMB 50 million. The net amount after offsetting these two amounts should be taken as RMB 50 million, to be paid by Party B by lending to the target company in accordance with Article 6 of this agreement. After such payment is completed in accordance with this provision, if there are still amounts owed by the target company to Party A, Party A would handle them itself, and the target company would no longer be obligated to repay. The price of the acquisition target was RMB 320 million, to be paid by Party B in accordance with the method set out in Article 6 of this agreement. On the day following the signing of this agreement, Party B would pay RMB 300 million to Party A as an advance payment for the acquisition target. Within 2 business days after Party A and Party B complete the handover of official seals and documents as described in Article 8 of this agreement, Party B would pay the remaining balance of the acquisition target price, RMB 20 million, to Party A. Within 2 business days after the completion of the industrial and commercial change registration for the equity transfer in this transaction, Party B would pay RMB 30 million in cash to Party A through the target company, to be used to repay the amounts owed by the target company to Party A and its affiliates. Within 2 business days after Party A completes the registration of change of ownership for the land use rights and the original GSP building property (as shown in the disclosure list) that Party A contributed to Sanpu Company but for which ownership registration had not yet been completed, Party B would pay RMB 20 million in cash to Party A through the target company, to be used to repay the amounts owed by the target company to Party A and its affiliates. The financial statements of the target company are all true, accurate, and complete in accordance with the currently effective accounting system of China, and do not contain any false records. If Party A fails to provide Party B with relevant certificates, transaction documents, data, information, evidence, etc., proving that the assets have been contributed to the target company, causing losses to the target company or Party B, such losses shall be fully borne by Party A. In addition, clear stipulations were made regarding breach of contract. The equity acquisition price of RMB 320 million as agreed by the parties had been fully paid by Tibet Rong'en Company to Far East Wisdom Company. The industrial and change registration as agreed in the agreement was completed on November 17, 2015. The ownership of the property was changed on December 17, 2015, and the ownership of the land was changed on December 22, 2015.

Xining Intermediate People's Court held at first instance that the Equity Acquisition Agreement and its appendices signed by Far East Smart Company and Tibet Rongen Company were both the true expression of the parties' intentions, and their content was not illegal; therefore they should be valid, and both parties should perform their respective obligations in accordance with the principles of equality, voluntariness, and good faith as stipulated in the agreement. According to the content of the Equity Acquisition Agreement, it could be confirmed that the parties explicitly stipulated that the acquisition consideration for the target company, Sanpu Company, consisted of an equity acquisition price of RMB 320 million and an amount payable by the target company of RMB 50 million. In this regard, the parties also specified in the contract the payment conditions and deadlines for the total amount of RMB 370 million. The existing evidence could confirm that Tibet Rongen Company had paid the equity acquisition consideration of RMB 320 million in accordance with the agreement, and could also confirm that Far East Smart Company had completed the industrial and commercial registration change of the equity transfer and the change procedures for the relevant land ownership certificates of the target company as agreed. Therefore, Tibet Rongen Company should also perform its payment obligation for the amount payable by the target company of RMB 50 million in accordance with the agreement. However, Tibet Rongen Company failed to perform its payment obligation for the remaining amount, which constituted a breach of contract and should bear corresponding liability for breach. Far East Smart Company's claim for payment of the remaining amount of RMB 50 million was established and should be supported. Regarding the liquidated damages, Xining Intermediate People's Court, in its discretion, calculated them based on the one-year LPR of 3.85% announced by the National Interbank Funding Center on August 20, 2020, as authorized by the People's Bank of China, increased by 50% and then further increased by 30%. The court then ruled: (1) Tibet Rongen Company shall pay Far East Smart Company the amount of RMB 50 million payable under the Equity Acquisition Agreement within thirty days after the judgment takes effect; (2) For the RMB 30 million that Tibet Rongen Company should pay, from November 20, 2015 to July 31, 2016, liquidated damages shall be calculated at RMB 1,501,500 (RMB 30 million x annual interest rate 3.85% x 8 months / 12 x 1.5 x 1.3 = RMB 1,501,500), and interest from August 1, 2016 until the date the RMB 30 million is fully paid shall be calculated according to the above standard; for the RMB 20 million that Tibet Rongen Company should pay, from December 25, 2015 to July 31, 2016, liquidated damages shall be calculated at RMB 875,875 (RMB 20 million x annual interest rate 3.85% x 7 months / 12 x 1.5 x 1.3), and interest from August 1, 2016 until the date the RMB 20 million is fully paid shall be calculated according to the above standard; (3) Tibet Rongen Company shall pay Far East Smart Company other losses and litigation fee losses totaling RMB 10,282,448.78 within thirty days after the judgment takes effect; (4) Far East Smart Company's claim for Tibet Rongen Company to bear lawyer's fees of RMB 1,250,000 is dismissed. The court acceptance fee for the first instance of RMB 530,212.24 shall be borne by Far East Smart Company in the amount of RMB 106,042.45 and by Tibet Rongen Company in the amount of RMB 424,169.79.

After the above first-instance judgment of Xining Intermediate People's Court was rendered, both Far East Smart Company and Tibet Rongen Company were dissatisfied and appealed to Qinghai High People's Court. Far East Smart Company and Tibet Rongen Company had no objection to the facts found in the first instance, which Qinghai High People's Court confirmed. Regarding the issue of whether Tibet Rongen Company should pay Far East Smart Company RMB 50 million and how the liquidated damages should be determined, Qinghai High People's Court held that the main dispute between the parties was whether the amount of the equity transfer consideration involved in the case was RMB 320 million or RMB 370 million. According to the facts found, Article 6 of the Equity Acquisition Agreement, "Price and Other Expenses Payment Method," clearly stipulated the amounts that Tibet Rongen Company should pay to Far East Smart Company, namely: the day after the agreement was signed, Tibet Rongen Company would pay RMB 300 million as a prepayment for the acquisition target; within two working days after the handover procedures for official seals and certificates were completed, Tibet Rongen Company would pay the remaining acquisition target price of RMB 20 million; within two working days after the industrial and commercial registration change of the equity transfer, Tibet Rongen Company would pay RMB 30 million to Far East Smart Company through the target company for the repayment of amounts owed by the target company to Far East Smart Company and its related parties; within two working days after Far East Smart Company completed the ownership change registration for the land use rights and the original GSP Building property that it had injected into Sanpu Company but for which the ownership registration had not yet been completed, Tibet Rongen Company would pay RMB 20 million to Far East Smart Company through the target company for the repayment of the remaining amounts owed by the target company to Far East Smart Company and its related parties. Calculated from the above payment conditions, the total amount that Tibet Rongen Company should pay to Far East Smart Company was RMB 370 million, of which RMB 320 million was the equity acquisition price, and RMB 50 million was to be paid by Tibet Rongen Company through Sanpu Company for the repayment of amounts owed by the target company to Far East Smart Company and its related parties. This stipulation was specific and clear, with no ambiguity in understanding the contract content. Regardless of whether the amount was the equity acquisition consideration or other payable expenses, it did not affect Tibet Rongen Company's obligation to perform the payment according to the contract; Tibet Rongen Company should perform as agreed. Regarding Tibet Rongen Company's defense that the payment of RMB 50 million through Sanpu Company to Far East Smart Company and its related parties required the actual existence of a creditor-debtor relationship between the parties, according to Article 4.1 of the Equity Acquisition Agreement, as of the equity transfer date, the amount payable by the target company to Far East Smart Company and its related parties did not exceed RMB 100 million, and the amount payable by Far East Smart Company and its related parties to the target company was estimated not to exceed RMB 50 million. The net value after offsetting these two items should be taken as RMB 50 million, to be paid by Tibet Rongen Company by lending to the target company in accordance with Article 6 of this agreement. After such payment was completed, if there were still amounts owed by the target company to Far East Smart Company, Far East Smart Company would handle them itself, and the target company would no longer bear the repayment obligation. According to this stipulation, the RMB 50 million involved in the case was a provision for the settlement of the creditor-debtor relationship between Far East Smart Company and Sanpu Company, and it was agreed that Tibet Rongen Company would pay it. No additional conditions or prerequisites for payment were stipulated. Therefore, Tibet Rongen Company's defense that it was only obligated to lend to Sanpu Company and had no obligation to pay RMB 50 million to Far East Smart Company was inconsistent with the agreement and was not accepted. Regarding the determination of liquidated damages, Qinghai High People's Court held that the handling by Xining Intermediate People's Court was not improper. Therefore, the appeal was dismissed and the original judgment was affirmed. The court acceptance fee for the second instance of RMB 652,969.79 was borne by Far East Smart Company in the amount of RMB 228,800 and by Tibet Rongen Company in the amount of RMB 424,169.79.

In the first instance of this case, the parties submitted evidence in accordance with their claims. The court of first instance organized the parties to exchange and cross-examine the evidence. The court of first instance confirmed the evidence to which the parties had no objection and placed it on file.

The court of first instance found the facts as follows: Party A, Far East Smart Company, and Party B, Tibet Rongen Company, signed the Equity Acquisition Agreement on October 21, 2015. The agreement stipulated: "Party A transfers the acquisition target to Party B in accordance with this agreement, and Party B purchases the acquisition target from Party A in accordance with this agreement. The acquisition target under this agreement is the 100% equity of Sanpu Company held by Party A. The net assets of the target company as of the equity transfer date shall not be less than RMB 240 million; otherwise, Party A shall make up the difference to Party B. The total liabilities as of the equity transfer date shall not exceed RMB 120 million; otherwise, Party A shall pay off the difference on behalf of the target company. As of the equity transfer date, the amount payable by the target company to Party A and its related parties does not exceed RMB 100 million, and the amount payable by Party A and its related parties to the target company is estimated not to exceed RMB 50 million. The net value after offsetting these two items shall be taken as RMB 50 million, to be paid by Party B by lending to the target company in accordance with Article 6 of this agreement. After such payment is completed, if there are still amounts owed by the target company to Party A, Party A shall handle them itself, and the target company shall no longer bear the repayment obligation. The above data shall be based on Sanpu Company's financial statements. The price of the acquisition target is RMB 320 million, to be paid by Party B in accordance with the method stipulated in Article 6 of this agreement. On the day after this agreement is signed, Party B pays RMB 300 million to Party A as a prepayment for the acquisition target; within two working days after Party A and Party B complete the handover procedures for official seals and certificates as described in Article 8 of this agreement, Party B pays the remaining acquisition target price of RMB 20 million to Party A. Within two working days after the industrial and commercial registration change of the equity transfer for this transaction is completed, Party B pays RMB 30 million in cash to Party A through the target company, for the repayment of amounts owed by the target company to Party A and its related parties; within two working days after Party A ensures that the land use rights and the original GSP Building property (see disclosure list) that it has injected into Sanpu Company but for which the ownership registration has not yet been completed are registered with changed ownership, Party B pays RMB 20 million in cash to Party A through the target company, for the repayment of all remaining amounts owed by the target company to Party A and its related parties. After Party B has paid a total of RMB 50 million to Party A and its related parties through the target company as described in Sections 6.3 and 6.4, the target company no longer needs to pay any amounts to Party A and its related parties." Based on the Equity Acquisition Agreement, Far East Smart Company sued Tibet Rongen Company in Xining Intermediate People's Court. After Xining Intermediate People's Court rendered a first-instance judgment, both parties were dissatisfied and appealed to Qinghai High People's Court. Qinghai High People's Court dismissed the appeal and affirmed the original judgment. After the above judgment became effective, Sanpu Company filed a third-party revocation action with the court of first instance.

The court of first instance held that the focus of the dispute in this case was whether Sanpu Company had the right to file a third-party revocation action and whether the first and second items of Civil Judgment No. (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu 52 were erroneous, and whether the relevant part of Civil Judgment No. (2020) Qing Min Zhong 291 that upheld the above items was erroneous and should be revoked.

The court of first instance held that the Equity Acquisition Agreement signed by Far East Smart Company (Party A) and Tibet Rongen Company (Party B) stipulated: "As of the equity transfer date, the amount payable by the target company to Party A and its related parties does not exceed RMB 100 million, and the amount payable by Party A and its related parties to the target company is estimated not to exceed RMB 50 million. The net value after offsetting these two items shall be taken as RMB 50 million, to be paid by Party B by lending to the target company in accordance with Article 6 of this agreement. After such payment is completed, if there are still amounts owed by the target company to Party A, Party A shall handle them itself, and the target company shall no longer bear the repayment obligation. The above data shall be based on Sanpu Company's financial statements." The above content has three levels and presents the following problems: First, "As of the equity transfer date, the amount payable by Sanpu Company to Far East Smart Company and its related parties does not exceed RMB 100 million, and the amount payable by Far East Smart Company and its related parties to Sanpu Company is estimated not to exceed RMB 50 million. The net value after offsetting these two items shall be taken as RMB 50 million." Given that Sanpu Company and Far East Smart Company's related parties did not participate in the conclusion of the agreement, the determination of the above creditor-debtor relationships and amounts has a legal interest in relation to Sanpu Company and Far East Smart Company's related parties, and may harm the civil rights and interests of Sanpu Company and Far East Smart Company's related parties. Second, "Tibet Rongen Company lends to Sanpu Company to pay Far East Smart Company in accordance with Article 6 of this agreement." First, the establishment of a loan relationship requires the debtor to actively incur the debt. When Sanpu Company itself did not actively incur the debt, Far East Smart Company reached an agreement with Tibet Rongen Company for Tibet Rongen Company to lend to Sanpu Company, but the borrowed funds were not paid to Sanpu Company; rather, they were paid to Far East Smart Company through Sanpu Company. Far East Smart Company and Tibet Rongen Company, by agreeing to set a debt for Sanpu Company, harmed Sanpu Company's civil rights and interests. Second, a loan contract is a practical contract that requires a mutual agreement between the lender and the borrower, i.e., a loan agreement between the borrower, Sanpu Company, and the lender, Tibet Rongen Company, and actual payment. When Sanpu Company did not incur the debt and Tibet Rongen Company did not agree to lend the funds, Far East Smart Company had no right to require Tibet Rongen Company to lend to Sanpu Company to pay that amount to Far East Smart Company. Third, "The above data shall be based on Sanpu Company's financial statements." As of the conclusion of the oral argument in the first instance of this case, none of the parties had submitted Sanpu Company's financial statements, so the accuracy of the above data was not determined. Sanpu Company neither participated in the conclusion of the Equity Acquisition Agreement nor took part in the trial of Case (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu 52 and Case (2020) Qing Min Zhong 291. The court, during the trial, also did not investigate or verify whether Sanpu Company owed money and the amount of any debt. That is, in Case (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu 52 and Case (2020) Qing Min Zhong 291, the fact of whether Sanpu Company owed RMB 50 million to Far East Smart Company and its related parties was not clarified. The effective judgment, without clarifying the above legal relationships and facts such as whether debts existed between the parties and the amounts, erroneously relied on the stipulation of the Equity Acquisition Agreement to order Tibet Rongen Company to pay Far East Smart Company the amount of RMB 50 million payable under the Equity Acquisition Agreement and corresponding liquidated damages. Although the judgment ordered Tibet Rongen Company to pay Far East Smart Company RMB 50 million and liquidated damages, according to the agreement, this amount was to be lent by Tibet Rongen Company to Sanpu Company and paid to Far East Smart Company through Sanpu Company. When Tibet Rongen Company performed the effective judgment and paid the above amount to Far East Smart Company, Sanpu Company would face the risk of being pursued for reimbursement by Tibet Rongen Company. The effective judgment was erroneous and harmed Sanpu Company's civil rights and interests.

Pursuant to Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (2017 Revision), which provides that "Where a third party considers that it has an independent claim to the subject matter of the litigation between the parties, it has the right to bring an action. Where a third party does not have an independent claim to the subject matter of the litigation between the parties, but the outcome of the case has a legal interest in relation to it, it may apply to participate in the litigation, or the people's court may notify it to participate in the litigation. A third party for whom the people's court's judgment bears civil liability shall have the litigation rights and obligations of a party. Where a third party as prescribed in the preceding two paragraphs fails to participate in the litigation for reasons not attributable to itself, but has evidence proving that part or all of the content of the legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation document is erroneous, harming its civil rights and interests, it may, within six months from the date it knows or should know that its civil rights and interests have been harmed, bring an action with the people's court that rendered the judgment, ruling, or mediation document. After trial, if the claim is established, the people's court shall change or revoke the original judgment, ruling, or mediation document; if the claim is not established, the claim shall be dismissed." In Case (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu 52 and Case (2020) Qing Min Zhong 291, which were equity transfer disputes between Far East Smart Company and Tibet Rongen Company, Sanpu Company did not have an independent claim, but the outcome of the above cases had a legal interest in relation to Sanpu Company, making Sanpu Company a third party without independent claim rights. Part of the content of the judgments in Case (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu 52 and Case (2020) Qing Min Zhong 291 was erroneous and harmed Sanpu Company's civil rights and interests. Sanpu Company had the right to bring a third-party revocation action within six months from the date the second-instance judgment in the original action was rendered (March 12, 2021). Regarding Far East Smart Company's defense that Sanpu Company knew about Case (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu 52 and Case (2020) Qing Min Zhong 291 but did not apply to participate in the litigation, and therefore did not meet the requirement of "failure to participate in the litigation for reasons not attributable to itself," so the action should be dismissed. The court of first instance held that "failure to participate in the litigation for reasons not attributable to oneself" generally refers to situations where the third party did not participate in the original litigation without obvious fault, i.e., the third party's failure to participate in the original litigation was not intentional or due to gross negligence. A third party without independent claim rights does not have an independent claim to the subject matter of the litigation, and the outcome of the case has a legal interest in relation to it. Therefore, during the process of the litigation and before the outcome is determined, it is usually difficult to judge. Even if a third party without independent claim rights knows that the litigation exists, if the people's court does not notify it to participate in the litigation and the parties do not apply for it to participate, its failure to apply to participate generally cannot be deemed as having obvious fault. Considering that the legal knowledge and litigation capabilities of litigants in China are currently not sufficiently high, requiring the third party to have no fault would be detrimental to protecting the lawful rights and interests of third parties outside the case. Therefore, the court of first instance did not support Far East Smart Company's defense.

In summary, the court of first instance held that Sanpu Company, as a third party with no independent claim, had a legal interest in the outcome of the case. Items 1 and 2 of the civil judgment (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 52 were erroneous, and the civil judgment (2020) Qing Min Zhong No. 291, which affirmed the aforementioned items, was partially erroneous and infringed upon Sanpu Company's civil rights and interests, and thus should be revoked. Pursuant to Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (2017 Revision) and Articles 292, 295, 296, 298, and 300 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (2020 Revision), the judgment is as follows: (1) Items 1 and 2 of the civil judgment (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 52 of the Xining Intermediate People's Court are revoked, namely: "1. Tibet Rong'en Company shall pay Far East Wisdom Company the amount of RMB 50,000,000 due under the Equity Acquisition Agreement within thirty days after the judgment takes effect; 2. For the RMB 30,000,000 payable by Tibet Rong'en Company, from November 20, 2015, to July 31, 2016, the liquidated damages shall be calculated based on the one-year LPR of 3.85% published by the National Interbank Funding Center on August 20, 2020, as authorized by the People's Bank of China, with a 50% increase and then an additional 30% increase, resulting in liquidated damages of RMB 1,501,500 (RMB 30,000,000 × annual interest rate 3.85% × 8 months ÷ 12 × 1.5 × 1.3 = RMB 1,501,500); interest from August 1, 2016, until the date of full payment of the RMB 30,000,000 shall be calculated according to the above standard; for the RMB 20,000,000 payable by Tibet Rong'en Company, from December 25, 2015, to July 31, 2016, the liquidated damages shall be calculated based on the one-year LPR of 3.85% published by the National Interbank Funding Center on August 20, 2020, as authorized by the People's Bank of China, with a 50% increase and then an additional 30% increase, resulting in liquidated damages of RMB 875,875 (RMB 20,000,000 × annual interest rate 3.85% × 7 months ÷ 12 × 1.5 × 1.3); interest from August 1, 2016, until the date of full payment of the RMB 20,000,000 shall be calculated according to the above standard." (2) The portion of the civil judgment (2020) Qing Min Zhong No. 291 of the Qinghai High People's Court that affirmed Items 1 and 2 of the civil judgment (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 52 is revoked. The court acceptance fee of RMB 291,800 for the first instance shall be borne by Far East Wisdom Company (RMB 145,900) and Tibet Rong'en Company (RMB 145,900).

During the second instance, Far East Wisdom Company submitted four sets of evidence, and this court organized the parties for evidence exchange and cross-examination.

First set of evidence: The Equity Acquisition Agreement filed with the Administration for Industry and Commerce when Sanpu Company's shareholders changed from Far East Wisdom Company to Tibet Rong'en Company, proving that Sanpu Company was responsible for handling the shareholder registration change with the Administration for Industry and Commerce and was fully aware of the entire content of the Equity Acquisition Agreement.

Second set of evidence: The civil judgment (2016) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 253, the civil ruling (2016) Qing Min Zhong Zi No. 163, and the civil judgment (2018) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 66, proving that when Far East Wisdom Company filed a lawsuit with the Xining Intermediate People's Court in July 2016 concerning the RMB 50,000,000 in dispute, the legal representatives of Sanpu Company and Tibet Rong'en Company were both Zhang Xuefeng, and Zhang Xuefeng was the signatory of the Equity Acquisition Agreement; Xu Yuanyuan, the current legal representative of Sanpu Company, participated in the trial of the related case; the two successive legal representatives of Sanpu Company were fully aware of the litigation between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company; the agent ad litem appointed by Tibet Rong'en Company in the second instance of this case is the same agent ad litem appointed by Sanpu Company in another case; Sanpu Company could make a clear judgment on whether the original judgment was adverse to its interests or infringed upon its lawful rights and interests; Sanpu Company had been aware of the relevant judgment results since 2016 and had not participated in the litigation after the case was remanded for retrial, thus failing to exercise its litigation rights and losing the qualification to file a third-party revocation action.

Third set of evidence: The civil judgment (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 40, the list of evidence and evidence 2 (balance sheet) submitted by Tibet Rong'en Company during the litigation of Far East Wisdom Company v. Tibet Rong'en Company concerning the RMB 50,000,000, proving that the RMB 50,000,000 debt was calculated based on audit of Sanpu Company's balance sheet and other financial data, and the amount that Sanpu Company should pay to Far East Wisdom Company is RMB 50,000,000.

Fourth set of evidence: The notice of response, notice of evidence submission, statement of claim, and service receipt served by the court of first instance in this case, proving that the court of first instance violated the filing procedures for accepting a third-party revocation action as stipulated in Article 293 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (2020 Revision), constituting procedural violation.

Regarding the evidence submitted by Far East Wisdom Company, Sanpu Company acknowledged the authenticity of the above industrial and commercial registration and relevant legal documents, but did not accept their probative purpose. It claimed ignorance of the evidence materials submitted by Tibet Rong'en Company in other cases and also did not accept the probative purpose of such evidence.

Tibet Rong'en Company acknowledged the authenticity of all the above evidence but did not accept their probative purpose.

Since the relevant evidence list in the third set of evidence was presented in another case and Tibet Rong'en Company has acknowledged its authenticity, this court confirms the fact that Sanpu Company's balance sheet in the other case had been submitted as evidence. The facts regarding Sanpu Company's change of industrial and commercial registration, the process of the litigation between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company regarding the equity transfer dispute, and the filing process of this case by the court of first instance are confirmed. The relevance of the above facts to this case will be explained in the reasoning section in conjunction with the issues in dispute.

This court finds the following facts during the second instance:

(1) Facts concerning Sanpu Company's change of industrial and commercial registration. On November 17, 2015, Sanpu Company's shareholders changed from Far East Wisdom Company to Tibet Rong'en Company, and the filing materials for the change of industrial and commercial registration included the Equity Acquisition Agreement between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company.

(2) Circumstances of other related litigations. 1. The original effective judgment that Sanpu Company seeks to revoke in this case is the equity transfer dispute between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company. Far East Wisdom Company filed a lawsuit with the Xining Intermediate People's Court on July 4, 2016, and on September 20, 2016, the Xining Intermediate People's Court rendered the civil judgment (2016) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 253. After the judgment was pronounced, both parties appealed to the Qinghai High People's Court. On December 14, 2016, the Qinghai High People's Court rendered the civil ruling (2016) Qing Min Zhong Zi No. 163, revoking the original judgment and remanding the case for retrial on the ground of unclear factual findings. On September 3, 2020, the Xining Intermediate People's Court rendered the civil judgment (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 52. After the judgment was pronounced, both parties appealed to the Qinghai High People's Court. On March 12, 2021, the Qinghai High People's Court rendered the civil judgment (2020) Qing Min Zhong No. 291, which is the effective judgment that the parties dispute whether it should be revoked in this case. During the first instance trial before the retrial, the legal representative of Tibet Rong'en Company, Zhang Xuefeng, was also the legal representative of Sanpu Company.

2. In the case of Sanpu Company v. Far East Wisdom Company regarding a shareholder capital contribution dispute, the Xining Intermediate People's Court accepted the case on November 8, 2016, and rendered the civil judgment (2016) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 370 on August 16, 2017. Sanpu Company appealed, and the Qinghai High People's Court rendered the civil ruling (2017) Qing Min Zhong No. 187 on January 11, 2018, remanding the case for retrial. On December 28, 2018, the Xining Intermediate People's Court rendered the civil judgment (2018) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 66. Sanpu Company appealed. The Qinghai High People's Court rendered the civil ruling (2019) Qing Min Zhong No. 89 on May 29, 2019, again remanding the case for retrial. On July 7, 2021, the Xining Intermediate People's Court rendered the civil judgment (2019) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 373. Sanpu Company appealed but later withdrew the appeal. The Qinghai High People's Court rendered the civil ruling (2021) Qing Min Zhong No. 212 on December 24, 2021, permitting Sanpu Company to withdraw the appeal. During the trial of this case, the court lawfully ascertained the circumstances of the litigation between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company in the case (2016) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 253.

3. In the case of Tibet Rong'en Company v. Far East Wisdom Company regarding an equity transfer dispute, the Xining Intermediate People's Court accepted the case on February 17, 2017. In this case, Tibet Rong'en Company claimed that there was a shortfall in the assets of Sanpu Company transferred by Far East Wisdom Company, and requested that Far East Wisdom Company make up the difference and pay liquidated damages, totaling over RMB 18.35 million. On September 3, 2020, the Xining Intermediate People's Court rendered the civil judgment (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 40, dismissing Tibet Rong'en Company's claims. Tibet Rong'en Company appealed. The Qinghai High People's Court rendered the civil ruling (2020) Qing Min Zhong No. 289 on January 28, 2021, remanding the case for retrial. This case is still pending. During the trial of the above case (2017) Qing 01 Min Chu No. 40, Tibet Rong'en Company submitted the balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement of Sanpu Company provided by Far East Wisdom Company to Tibet Rong'en Company, and Tibet Rong'en Company submitted relevant financial accounting vouchers of Sanpu Company in that case.

The remaining facts found in the second instance are consistent with those in the first instance.

Opinion of the Court:

Pursuant to Article 1, Paragraph 2 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Temporal Effect of the Application of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China: "For civil dispute cases arising from legal facts that occurred before the implementation of the Civil Code, the provisions of the laws and judicial interpretations in effect at that time shall apply, except as otherwise provided by law or judicial interpretation," the facts in dispute in this case occurred before the implementation of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, so the laws and judicial interpretations in effect at that time shall apply. Based on the parties' appeal requests and responses, the main issues in dispute in this case are: (1) Whether Sanpu Company is a third party with no independent claim in the original effective judgment case; (2) Whether the original effective judgment infringed upon Sanpu Company's rights and interests and whether it should be revoked; (3) Whether Sanpu Company's failure to participate in the trial of the original effective judgment case was due to reasons not attributable to itself; (4) Whether there was a major procedural violation in the acceptance procedure of the first instance.

(1) Regarding whether Sanpu Company is a third party with no independent claim in the original effective judgment case.

This court holds that Sanpu Company may lawfully serve as a third party with no independent claim in the original effective judgment case. The reasons are as follows:

First, although the parties to the Equity Acquisition Agreement are Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company, the subject matter of the transaction is the 100% equity of Sanpu Company held by Far East Wisdom Company. Sanpu Company is the target company of the equity transfer transaction, and this transaction inevitably affected the operation and management of Sanpu Company. The result of the trial of the equity transfer dispute has a legal interest with Sanpu Company. Sanpu Company may lawfully participate in the litigation as a third party with no independent claim.

Second, from the content of the Equity Acquisition Agreement, the RMB 50,000,000 debt stipulated in Article 4.1 was determined after the new and old shareholders of Sanpu Company calculated the claims and debts between Sanpu Company and Far East Wisdom Company and its affiliates, and it was agreed that the transferee shareholder, Tibet Rong'en Company, would pay this amount. This agreement constitutes a debt assumption by Tibet Rong'en Company to Sanpu Company. At the same time, the agreement also provides that Tibet Rong'en Company would lend the RMB 50,000,000 to Sanpu Company, and Sanpu Company would pay it to Far East Wisdom Company. According to the performance method agreed in the agreement, Far East Wisdom Company has the right to require Tibet Rong'en Company and Sanpu Company to perform in this manner. Therefore, this performance method actually imposes an obligation on Sanpu Company. In the original equity transfer dispute, whether Far East Wisdom Company filed a lawsuit requesting or the court ordered the parties to perform the RMB 50,000,000 debt in the manner agreed in the agreement has a legal interest with Sanpu Company. Sanpu Company may lawfully participate in the equity transfer litigation between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company as a third party with no independent claim. Far East Wisdom Company's argument that the Equity Acquisition Agreement is unrelated to Sanpu Company, does not involve Sanpu Company's rights and interests, and that Sanpu Company is not a third party with no independent claim lacks a basis and is untenable under the law.

(2) Regarding whether the original effective judgment infringed upon Sanpu Company's rights and interests and whether it should be revoked.

This court holds that although Sanpu Company could participate in the original effective judgment case as a third party with no independent claim, given that Sanpu Company did not participate in the litigation, the original effective judgment did not infringe upon Sanpu Company's rights and interests. The reasons are as follows:

First, the essence of the Equity Acquisition Agreement is the payment of equity consideration and the delivery of equity. As the target of the transaction, Sanpu Company cannot prevent or restrict the equity transfer in question. Although the equity transfer price agreed in the agreement was RMB 320,000,000, Article 4.1 stipulates: "As of the date of equity transfer, the amount payable by the target company to Party A and its affiliates shall not exceed RMB 100,000,000, and the amount payable by Party A and its affiliates to the target company is estimated not to exceed RMB 50,000,000. The net amount after offsetting these two items shall be valued at RMB 50,000,000." "Party B shall lend the money to the target company for payment in accordance with Article 6 of this agreement. After payment is made in accordance with this provision, if there are still amounts owed by the target company to Party A, Party A shall handle them on its own, and the target company shall no longer bear the obligation to repay. The above data shall be based on Sanpu Company's financial statements." That is, the transferee shall assume the target company's debt of RMB 50,000,000 to the transferring shareholder and its affiliates, and it is agreed that after assuming this RMB 50,000,000, if the target company still has debts exceeding RMB 50,000,000, the transferring shareholder cannot claim against the target company. This clause is a provision for the confirmation and settlement of the target company's prior debts by the parties to the equity transfer, representing a comprehensive solution for the relevant claims and debts, and it is agreed that Tibet Rong'en Company shall pay this amount to Far East Wisdom Company. This RMB 50,000,000 should be lawfully recognized as part of the equity transfer consideration. Although this RMB 50,000,000 was calculated based on the debts of Sanpu Company by both parties, whether this amount as equity transfer consideration is true or whether it is manifestly unfair falls within the scope of Tibet Rong'en Company's right to exercise the right of revocation under the law and is unrelated to Sanpu Company. Therefore, Sanpu Company's claim that the agreement additionally imposed debts on it lacks a basis.

Second, based on the facts found in this case, Sanpu Company should have known about the Equity Acquisition Agreement. At the time the Equity Acquisition Agreement was signed, the sole shareholder of Sanpu Company was Far East Wisdom Company, and Far East Wisdom Company handled Sanpu Company's accounts, so Sanpu Company should have known. The intended transferee shareholder, Tibet Rong'en Company, was also the future 100% shareholder of Sanpu Company, and the legal representative of Tibet Rong'en Company who signed the Equity Acquisition Agreement was also the legal representative of Sanpu Company after the equity transfer. Therefore, whether before or after the equity transfer, Sanpu Company should have known about the equity transfer in question. After the equity transfer, Sanpu Company handled the change of industrial and commercial registration in accordance with the agreement and filed the Equity Acquisition Agreement as part of the industrial and commercial registration materials. Sanpu Company's claim that it did not participate in the signing of the agreement and that the parties to the agreement unilaterally imposed obligations on it is inconsistent with the facts and is untenable under the law.

Third, Article 6 of the Equity Acquisition Agreement provides that the RMB 50,000,000 in question shall be lent by Tibet Rong'en Company to Sanpu Company, and then Sanpu Company shall pay it to Far East Wisdom Company. This clause indeed imposes a performance obligation on Sanpu Company. However, as discussed above, the RMB 50,000,000 is the equity transfer consideration between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rong'en Company, and the obligor for payment is Tibet Rong'en Company. This provision should be the method of performance for the RMB 50,000,000. Since Tibet Rong'en Company did not lend the money to Sanpu Company as agreed, and Sanpu Company did not pay Far East Wisdom Company, when Tibet Rong'en Company failed to perform the payment in the manner agreed in the contract, Far East Wisdom Company sued Tibet Rong'en Company for direct performance based on breach of contract. Far East Wisdom Company did not request in the original lawsuit that Sanpu Company make the payment as per the agreement. The original effective judgment, based on Far East Wisdom Company's claims, tried the case and lawfully ordered Tibet Rong'en Company to continue paying RMB 50,000,000 to Far East Wisdom Company and bear liability for breach of contract. The reasoning and the judgment items neither impose obligations nor liabilities on Sanpu Company. Therefore, the original effective judgment does not infringe upon Sanpu Company's rights and interests and should not be revoked. Sanpu Company's claim that the original effective judgment would inevitably lead to Tibet Rong'en Company seeking recourse against Sanpu Company lacks a basis and is untenable under the law. The first instance judgment's finding that the Equity Acquisition Agreement imposed a RMB 50,000,000 loan debt on Sanpu Company, and that the loan had not been performed, thus concluding that the original effective judgment might infringe upon Sanpu Company's rights and interests, was erroneous in fact and is corrected by this court in accordance with the law.

Finally, regarding the RMB 50,000,000 debt, although the agreement provides "based on financial statements," the parties did not submit a document titled "financial statements" during either the first or second instance. However, Tibet Rong'en Company acknowledged the financial audit report of Sanpu Company submitted by Far East Wisdom Company. The attachments to the audit report are Sanpu Company's balance sheet, income statement, and other financial data, which already reflect Sanpu Company's asset and liability situation. From the circumstances of the related cases filed by Sanpu Company and Tibet Rong'en Company against Far East Wisdom Company, the claims of Sanpu Company after the equity transfer are consistent with those of Tibet Rong'en Company. Therefore, Sanpu Company's claim in this case that the parties did not submit financial statements after the equity transfer and that Sanpu Company's accounts are uncertain is inconsistent with the facts and should not be supported under the law. Additionally, regarding the original effective judgment, Tibet Rong'en Company has applied to this court for retrial, and its opinions on the original effective judgment are no longer addressed in this case.

(3) Regarding whether Sanpu Company's failure to participate in the trial of the original effective judgment case was due to reasons not attributable to itself.

This court holds that Sanpu Company does not fall within the circumstance of "failure to participate in the litigation due to reasons not attributable to itself" as stipulated in Article 59, Paragraph 3 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China for a third-party revocation action. The reasons are as follows:

Upon investigation, the dispute over equity transfer between Far East Wisdom Company and Tibet Rongen Company underwent two trials in the Xining Intermediate People's Court and the Qinghai High People's Court, with the proceedings from July 4, 2016 to March 12, 2021. When the Xining Intermediate People's Court held a hearing in 2016, the legal representatives of both Tibet Rongen Company and Sanpu Company were Zhang Xuefeng, and Tibet Rongen Company was the 100% controlling shareholder of Sanpu Company, so it could be legally determined that Sanpu Company was aware of the proceedings of the original lawsuit. Although Sanpu Company argued that before the effective judgment in the original lawsuit was rendered, it was difficult to determine whether the outcome of the case had a legal interest to it, and thus could not be deemed to have clear fault, as stated in the second disputed issue above, Sanpu Company was fully aware of the signing process and content of the Equity Transfer Agreement involved in the case. It raised no objection during the signing and performance of the agreement. Moreover, during the trial of the original lawsuit, Tibet Rongen Company had already raised the defense that the debt was untrue and the amount was incorrect, which was essentially no different from Sanpu Company's defense in this case. If Sanpu Company believed that its rights might be infringed, it knew or should have known of the infringement when Tibet Rongen Company raised the defense, but it did not apply to participate in the proceedings to assert its claims, indicating that it either accepted or condoned the separate trial and judgment. Sanpu Company's claim that it could only know whether its rights were damaged after the judgment became effective is inconsistent with the facts and cannot be legally established. The first-instance judgment found that Sanpu Company did not participate in the proceedings due to reasons not attributable to itself, which was erroneous in fact-finding and misapplication of law, and this court hereby corrects it according to law.

(4) Whether there are serious procedural violations in the first-instance acceptance procedure

Pursuant to Article 291 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, in a third-party revocation action case, the people's court shall, within five days from the date of receipt of the complaint and evidence materials, serve them on the opposing party, and the opposing party may submit a written opinion within ten days from the date of receipt of the complaint. The people's court shall review the complaint, evidence materials submitted by the third party, and the written opinion of the opposing party. Where necessary, it may inquire of both parties. Upon review, if the conditions for filing are met, the people's court shall file the case within thirty days from the date of receipt of the complaint. If the conditions are not met, it shall rule within thirty days from the date of receipt of the complaint to reject the filing.

Upon investigation, the first-instance court did not serve the complaint on Far East Wisdom Company before filing the case, which indeed constitutes a defect in the filing review for the third-party revocation action. However, this court considers that after the filing of this case, Far East Wisdom Company has participated in the trial process, and the first-instance court has ensured opportunities for both parties to present statements and debate, without prejudicing the parties' right to express opinions. Therefore, it does not affect the handling of this case according to law and does not constitute a serious procedural violation. Far East Wisdom Company's ground of appeal on this issue cannot be established, and this court does not support it according to law.

In summary, Far East Wisdom Company's above claims are established. The first-instance judgment had errors in fact-finding and misapplication of law, which this court hereby corrects. Pursuant to Article 59 and subparagraph 2 of Article 177(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2021) Qing Min Che No. 1 of the Qinghai High People's Court;

2. Dismiss the claims of Sanpu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 291,800 and the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 291,800 shall both be borne by Sanpu Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
